dedupe_keys.name: audio datasets of belt conveyor rollers in mines normal shell cracking breakage

description: This figshare dataset holds audio recordings of belt conveyor rollers working at a mining site, in three conditions: normal operation, roller shell cracking and complete roller breakage. The DataCite record says there are 19 WAV files from 19 microphones, 17 of normal rollers, one of a cracked shell and one of a broken roller, plus audio feature tables extracted with frame lengths from 100 ms to 1,000 ms, a 200 ms test set and the machine-learning code. It was published on 19 September 2024 by Juan Liu, Shiming Fu, Fen Liu and Xuefeng Cheng, with a total size of about 1.3 GB, downloadable from figshare and free under CC BY 4.0 (the record has versions 1 and 2 under the same DOI root). Coverage is one mine conveyor; the mine, its country and the recording dates are not stated on the page read. Caveats: only two fault recordings exist, so classes are very unbalanced, and the page warns that feature sets with different frame lengths must not be mixed. For simulation it supports condition-monitoring and predictive-maintenance models for bulk material handling, and gives failure signatures to drive component failure events in mine and port conveyor digital twins. Related catalogue records include the NASA Prognostics data repository, the Sirris injection moulding drying faults data and the Global supply chain logistics excavator data.
